Definition: from the same as G4613; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites:--Simeon, Simon.
BiblicalUsage: Simeon is the just and devout man in Jerusalem who waits for the consolation of Israel, with the Holy Ghost upon him, and when he takes the child Jesus in his arms he blesses God and tells Mary the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel. The same name belongs to Simeon called Niger at Antioch, to Simon Peter whom James calls Symeon when he tells how God first visited the Gentiles, to the Simeon of the genealogy, and to the tribe of Simeon.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that Simeon shows me how to wait: just, devout, and listening until God puts the promise in his arms. I hold that a life spent waiting on God is never wasted, because He keeps His word to those who wait.
